## PR Description

Closes #852
## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

## References

gh-848 (minter + orphan law comments), gh-842, fa #1457 (five resets, full timelines), gh-850 (latch gap).

## PR Description

Closes #852
## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

## References

gh-848 (minter + orphan law comments), gh-842, fa #1457 (five resets, full timelines), gh-850 (latch gap).

## PR Description

Closes #852
## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

## References

gh-848 (minter + orphan law comments), gh-842, fa #1457 (five resets, full timelines), gh-850 (latch gap).

## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

gh-848 (minter + orphan law comments), gh-842, fa #1457 (five resets, full timelines), gh-850 (latch gap).

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-852` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +695
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T12:54:25Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T12:54:25Z

## PR Description

Closes #852
## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

## References

gh-848 (minter + orphan law comments), gh-842, fa #1457 (five resets, full timelines), gh-850 (latch gap).

## PR Description

## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

blocks.text:
Now I understand the flow. Let me check some helper functions:

1. `headCheckRunsSafe` — the transport. Does it use ioCache? Multiple `headPlaceholders` calls per tick (green-cover guard, latch guard, gate) — each is a separate fetch of check runs for the same head. In the gate path, when green-cover void fires via zombies (gh-842 case), placeholders are not probed (gGreenPh only computed when no zombies). In the placeholder path, headCheckRunZombies is called (guard) then headPlaceholders (gate) — two check-run fetches. Is there caching? Let me check headCheckRunsSafe and whether there's an ioCache.

2. `silentUpdateBranch` — check its semantics (merge latest main / empty commit).

3. `repoPoolFree` — uses `github_list_workflow_runs` with perPage: 50 — check the tool signature to see if it filters by status or branch. If it lists ALL runs repo-wide sorted by created desc, 50 is probably enough for "any ACTIVE run" — active runs are recent. OK.

4. Check `validationLivenessModule.ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` — verify that module has ACTIVE_RUN_STATES. Actually checkRunZombies.js exports ACTIVE_RUN_STATES; is validationLivenessModule the same? Let me check imports in smAgent.js.

5. Important logic check: `repoPoolFree` — the probe happens after cap check but before DRY check. In DRY mode it still performs pool probe (API call). Minor.

6. Bigger logic concern: the placeholder gate is evaluated on every validate_pr dispatch, including rules that are NOT skipIfGreenCi. Consider: the PR has placeholders on its head; the head otherwise has no green; flow reaches dispatch gate; placeholder gate fires → fresh-sha reset. That matches AC1.

But a subtle issue: after the reset + dispatch on the new head, the new dispatch could queue again → mints fresh placeholders ~20s later. The pool-free probe is supposed to prevent this. OK.

Another subtle issue: the check-run "placeholder" detection uses `started_at` of the check-run. GitHub placeholder check-runs have `started_at` — fine.

7. Potential concern: `headPlaceholders` in the green-cover guard only runs when `gGreenZombies.zombies.length === 0`. If the head has BOTH zombies (run-id ghosts) and placeholders, the zombie branch fires with legacy re-dispatch (AC3-ish). Hmm — per ticket, placeholders need fresh-sha; but mixed case falls to legacy dispatch. Edge case, probably acceptable but the PR says "Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3)". A mixed head would get same-sha re-dispatch, which re-mints placeholders if queued... but pool probe isn't consulted there either. This is a design nuance — probably fine as suggestion-level.

8. `failMarkerState` is called in the gate on every tick when placeholders detected — it fetches PR comments. Was already fetched for redHeadBlocked? Actually redHeadBlocked is a separate path. failMarkerState fetches comments each time. OK, existing pattern.

9. Marker regex: `🔁 placeholder reset (\d+)\/(\d+) at (\S+)` with the `g` flag and lastIndex reset per body — good.

10. Park marker constant: `'\uD83C\uDFF7\uFE0F Placeholder resets capped'` — 🏷️ Placeholder resets capped. Note in test they check `body.indexOf('Placeholder resets capped') !== -1`. Fine.

11. Check: `placeholderParked` once-per-cap-hit — but the marker check is substring over all comment bodies; if a park note was posted in a PREVIOUS window, `placeholderParked` stays true forever, so a future cap-hit in a new window won't post a new park note. Is that intended? "say so ONCE" — the intent may be once per cap event. Minor issue: after the window resets (2h quiet), the count goes to 0; if placeholders persist and resets burn the cap again, no new park note is posted because placeholderParked is true from the old note. This is a minor observability gap — SUGGESTION level. Actually arguably intended ("say so ONCE"). I'd note as suggestion.

12. Now the cap check ordering issue: gate does cap check BEFORE pool probe and DRY check. In DRY mode, `failMarkerState` reads comments — fine.

13. Verify `github_list_workflow_runs` exists as a global in smAgent environment (mcp tool). Grep for its usage elsewhere.

14. Check tests run. Let me run the unit tests for the two files.

15. Check `validationLivenessModule` import — line references `validationLivenessModule.ACTIVE_RUN_STATES`.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

## References

gh-848 (minter + orphan law comments), gh-842, fa #1457 (five resets, full timelines), gh-850 (latch gap).

## PR Description

## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T12:54:25Z

## PR Description

Closes #852
## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

## References

gh-848 (minter + orphan law comments), gh-842, fa #1457 (five resets, full timelines), gh-850 (latch gap).

## PR Description

Closes #852
## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

## References

gh-848 (minter + orphan law comments), gh-842, fa #1457 (five resets, full timelines), gh-850 (latch gap).

Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. ## PR Description

## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).
