# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

This PR adds up to 2-3 more sequential rounds in the placeholder-pinned path. Suggest caching the rollup per (head) per tick. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? It costs API rounds on a hot path; the gh-842 work explicitly reduced rounds. I'd say IMPORTANT leaning SUGGESTION... It's a real perf regression in the exact pathological case only (placeholder-pinned PRs, which are rare and capped). And gate path only when placeholders detected. Actually green-cover guard path: for every skipIfGreenCi green PR, one extra check-run fetch per tick (headPlaceholders only when no zombies — zombies fetched first anyway which pre-existed). The added cost is 1 extra fetch per green PR per tick in the common case. SUGGESTION.

2. **Mixed zombie+placeholder head falls to legacy same-sha dispatch** (SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT): guards only probe placeholders when `zombies.length === 0`. A head carrying both a run-id ghost AND a placeholder would take the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch, which can never cure the placeholder and may re-mint placeholders. Real? A head with a cancelled run ghost + placeholders is plausible (dispatch queued → placeholders minted; prior run cancelled). Design decision documented? The PR description says "Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3)" — deliberate for pure run-id ghosts. But mixed case silently picks the weaker remedy. IMPORTANT? Hmm. In mixed case, the legacy re-dispatch fires: if it materializes immediately, its fresh stamps override both ghosts (latest per context) — including placeholders IF the stamped contexts match the placeholder names. The placeholders carry names of required checks (e.g., 'Quality gate'), and stamped names are validationCheckNames() — likely same names. So same-sha dispatch with immediate start could cure. But if it queues, fresh placeholders re-minted. It's a partial-coverage edge case. I'd classify SUGGESTION (or low IMPORTANT). I'll go SUGGESTION with clear rationale.

3. **`hasPlaceholderZombies` exported but unused in production** (SUGGESTION): dead API surface — only the test references it. Either wire it into the gate (e.g., use in classify partition) or drop it.

Next tick re-detects placeholders, burns another cap. Edge case: branch already contains main but placeholders persist. Mitigated by pool probe (immediate-start dispatch cures). Still, counting an un-minted reset against the cap could burn the budget without a head move. Hmm — is that reachable? validate rules exclude BEHIND PRs; a PR whose branch already contains main and is not BEHIND... "already up to date" means main is ancestor of HEAD — that IS up-to-date (not BEHIND). So yes reachable: placeholders on a fresh-up-to-date head → silent update no-ops → same-sha dispatch (pool-free, so likely immediate start; run stamps override placeholders). If it materializes, cured. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

💡 **SUGGESTION: `hasPlaceholderZombies` is exported but never used in production code**

`hasPlaceholderZombies` (js/common/checkRunZombies.js:238) is added to the public API and tested, but no production code path calls it — the smAgent gate probes placeholders directly via `headPlaceholders()`/`placeholders()` and treats run-id ghosts via `vPh.length === 0`. Either wire it into the decision (e.g. let a mixed zombie+placeholder head explicitly prefer the fresh-sha path in the guard log) or drop the export to keep the module surface minimal. Not blocking — dead weight only.

💡 **SUGGESTION: up to 3 redundant check-run fetches per tick for the same head**

In the placeholder-pinned path, the same head's check-run rollup is fetched up to 3 times in one tick: `headPlaceholders` at the green-cover guard (line 2019), the latch-skip guard (line 2092), and the dispatch gate (line 2322). `headCheckRunsSafe` performs an uncached `github_get_commit_check_runs` REST call each time — and the bundle comment a few lines above (the gh-842 work) explicitly says "ONE probe bundle feeds every guard below (was up to 4 sequential gh api rounds per candidate)". This PR re-grows that round count by 2–3 on exactly the hot path. Consider caching the rollup per (head) for the tick (e.g. a small memo on `repoInfo` or a module-level `lastHeadRollup`) and reusing it across the three probes. Cheap to do and consistent with the existing round-reduction intent.

💡 **SUGGESTION: DRY check runs after real API reads**

The placeholder gate orders: cap check (`failMarkerState` → PR-comment fetch) → pool probe (`github_list_workflow_runs`, repo-wide) → **then** `if (DRY)`. A dry-run tick therefore still performs a comment read and a workflow-runs probe before logging "placeholder reset skipped". Compare `dispatchCiWorkflow`, which guards DRY internally at the top. Moving the DRY guard ahead of the cap/pool steps makes dry runs side-effect- and read-free, and matches the codebase's "DRY means NO side effects" contract.

💡 **SUGGESTION: park-note dedupe is sticky across windows**

`out.placeholderParked` is `true` if ANY historical comment contains `PLACEHOLDER_PARK_MARKER` — with no window scoping, unlike the marker count. After a quiet 2h restarts the budget and the PR burns the cap again, no new park note is posted (the operator sees silence the second time around). If "say so ONCE" was meant as once per cap-hit, scope the dedupe to a park note whose age is inside the current window (e.g. parse a timestamp from the note, same as `placeholderMarks` does for reset markers). If deliberate, a one-line comment stating "park note is intentionally once ever per PR" would prevent a future "fix".

💡 **SUGGESTION: a no-op silent update still consumes cap budget**

`silentUpdateBranch` exits 0 with "silent-update: already up to date" when the branch already contains main — the head does **not** move, yet the code then counts the reset (`placeholderMarkerLine(phMarks.count + 1, ...)`) and consumes cap budget for a fresh sha it never minted. This is reachable: a PR whose branch already contains main is not BEHIND, so validate rules still match it. The pool probe makes it mostly harmless (a free pool means the same-sha dispatch is likely to materialize and override the placeholders anyway), but if that dispatch queues despite the probe, the cap burns without the cure it exists to count. Since `phNewHead` is already re-read below, consider skipping the marker/arm-count when `phNewHead === vHead0` (log "silent update no-op — head unchanged, not counted" and fall through to a plain dispatch).

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-852` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +695
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-10-11T12:54:25Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-11T12:54:25Z

## PR Description

Closes #852
## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

## References

gh-848 (minter + orphan law comments), gh-842, fa #1457 (five resets, full timelines), gh-850 (latch gap).

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

## PR Description

Closes #852
## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

## References

gh-848 (minter + orphan law comments), gh-842, fa #1457 (five resets, full timelines), gh-850 (latch gap).

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

## PR Description

Closes #852
## gh-852: Check-run placeholders pin the merge gate — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe

### Root Cause
- Placeholder check-runs (pending, `html_url` with no numeric run id — minted ~20s after a dispatch that queued without materializing a job) pin `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`: branch protection takes the LATEST check-run per (context, head), so they shadow every green real check (live fa #1457: heads d29efb16 + 3 predecessors, 5 operator resets/day).
- The engine's only remedy was the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch — mechanically wrong here: a queued re-dispatch mints FRESH placeholders on the same sha. Only a fresh sha + an immediate-start validation cures the gate.

### Fix
- `js/common/checkRunZombies.js` (additive, AC3-safe): `placeholders()` — link-less pending stamps older than a 3-min grace (a fresh stamp may be a live dispatch's bridge stamp; only age proves no runner is coming); `hasPlaceholderZombies()` — the run-id-less zombie shape; per-PR windowed reset cap bookkeeping (`placeholderMarks`/`placeholderMarkerLine`/`placeholderRetryAllowed`/`placeholderCapOf`/`placeholderWindowMsOf`, default 3 per 2h — per PR, not per head: every reset mints a new head).
- `js/smAgent.js`:
  - green-cover and latch-skip guards: placeholder check-runs VOID the skip too (detected at the 3-min grace, not the 30-min zombie staleness);
  - placeholder gate at the validate_pr dispatch point: cap check (AC2) → repo pool-free probe via `github_list_workflow_runs` — no ACTIVE run repo-wide, the conservative macos/ubuntu-arm proxy; probe failure fails CLOSED (AC2) → `silentUpdateBranch` fresh-sha refresh → re-read new head → `dispatchCiWorkflow` on the branch → stamp the new head → re-arm `ai_validating` → marker comment. Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3).

### Test Coverage
- `js/unit-tests/test_checkRunZombies.js` — gh-852 suites: detection (incl. the d29efb16 replay: placeholder caught at the 3-min grace while `classify()` still reads it live), fail-safe young/unparseable stamps, knob tuning, cap bookkeeping round-trip.
- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — 4 new tests: AC1 placeholder-pinned green PR → exactly one silent-update refresh + one dispatch + arm + `placeholder reset 1/3` marker; AC2 busy pool → deferred, zero churn; AC2 cap reached → one park note, no resets; AC3 run-id zombie → legacy dispatch, no refresh.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — **2524 passed, 0 failed**.

### Notes
- The pool probe is deliberately conservative (any ACTIVE run repo-wide blocks a reset) — the ticket's macos/ubuntu-arm labels ride job objects, not the run list; it also subsumes the gh-798 in-flight-leg guard.
- On a failed validation dispatch after the refresh, the fresh sha stands and the next tick validates it normally (self-healing; the attempt is not cap-counted, matching the gh-821 zombie contract).
- New knobs: `checkRunPlaceholderMinutes` (default 3), `placeholderResetCap` (default 3), `placeholderResetWindowMs` (default 2h).

# gh-852: [GOAL] Check-run placeholders (no-cancel orphans) pin the merge gate on every queued dispatch — engine auto-reset on detection + pool-free probe (live fa #1457: 5 operator resets today)

## Description

## Goal

Engine-level auto-unblock for the check-run placeholder pathology: when a PR head carries placeholder check-runs (pending/in_progress check-runs whose html_url has no numeric run id — created by GitHub ~20s after dispatch when no job has materialized, orphaned when the real job later stamps its own check-run), the merge gate pins them (BLOCKED) even though every real check-run is green. Same-sha re-dispatch can NEVER fix this (the new dispatch mints new placeholders if it queues again); ONLY a fresh sha cures it — and then only if the next dispatch materializes its first job in <~10-20s.

## Rule

On placeholder detection (extend js/common/checkRunZombies.js): instead of (or in addition to) the gh-842 VOID re-dispatch, trigger a fresh-sha refresh of the PR (silent-update style: merge latest main / empty commit via the machine author) and dispatch validation on the NEW sha only when a pool-free probe says the run can start immediately (e.g., no in_progress macos/ubuntu-arm runs in the repo). Retry cap per PR per 2h to avoid reset storms.

## Live evidence

fa #1457 (2026-10-11): heads d29efb16 and 3 predecessors each show the pattern — real run 38137997380 all-green stamps at 12:08-12:18, placeholders at 12:06:29-31, mergeStateStatus BLOCKED. Merges succeed only when dispatch→first-job gap <~10s (all of today's successful merges). Operator resets cured the gate mechanically every time but the next queued dispatch re-minted placeholders (5 resets today).

## Acceptance

1. AC1: a placeholder-pinned green PR gets a fresh sha + a fast-start validation without operator action.
2. AC2: no reset storm (cap + pool probe).
3. AC3: the existing zombie/cancel rules keep working (placeholders are the no-cancel variant).

gh-848 (minter + orphan law comments), gh-842, fa #1457 (five resets, full timelines), gh-850 (latch gap).

Multiple `headPlaceholders` calls per tick (green-cover guard, latch guard, gate) — each is a separate fetch of check runs for the same head. In the gate path, when green-cover void fires via zombies (gh-842 case), placeholders are not probed (gGreenPh only computed when no zombies). In the placeholder path, headCheckRunZombies is called (guard) then headPlaceholders (gate) — two check-run fetches. Is there caching? Let me check headCheckRunsSafe and whether there's an ioCache.

2. `silentUpdateBranch` — check its semantics (merge latest main / empty commit).

3. `repoPoolFree` — uses `github_list_workflow_runs` with perPage: 50 — check the tool signature to see if it filters by status or branch. If it lists ALL runs repo-wide sorted by created desc, 50 is probably enough for "any ACTIVE run" — active runs are recent. OK.

4. Check `validationLivenessModule.ACTIVE_RUN_STATES` — verify that module has ACTIVE_RUN_STATES. Actually checkRunZombies.js exports ACTIVE_RUN_STATES; is validationLivenessModule the same? Let me check imports in smAgent.js.

5. Important logic check: `repoPoolFree` — the probe happens after cap check but before DRY check. In DRY mode it still performs pool probe (API call). Minor.

6. Bigger logic concern: the placeholder gate is evaluated on every validate_pr dispatch, including rules that are NOT skipIfGreenCi. Consider: the PR has placeholders on its head; the head otherwise has no green; flow reaches dispatch gate; placeholder gate fires → fresh-sha reset. That matches AC1.

But a subtle issue: after the reset + dispatch on the new head, the new dispatch could queue again → mints fresh placeholders ~20s later. The pool-free probe is supposed to prevent this. OK.

Another subtle issue: the check-run "placeholder" detection uses `started_at` of the check-run. GitHub placeholder check-runs have `started_at` — fine.

7. Potential concern: `headPlaceholders` in the green-cover guard only runs when `gGreenZombies.zombies.length === 0`. If the head has BOTH zombies (run-id ghosts) and placeholders, the zombie branch fires with legacy re-dispatch (AC3-ish). Hmm — per ticket, placeholders need fresh-sha; but mixed case falls to legacy dispatch. Edge case, probably acceptable but the PR says "Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3)". A mixed head would get same-sha re-dispatch, which re-mints placeholders if queued... but pool probe isn't consulted there either. This is a design nuance — probably fine as suggestion-level.

8. `failMarkerState` is called in the gate on every tick when placeholders detected — it fetches PR comments. Was already fetched for redHeadBlocked? Actually redHeadBlocked is a separate path. failMarkerState fetches comments each time. OK, existing pattern.

9. Marker regex: `🔁 placeholder reset (\d+)\/(\d+) at (\S+)` with the `g` flag and lastIndex reset per body — good.

10. Park marker constant: `'\uD83C\uDFF7\uFE0F Placeholder resets capped'` — 🏷️ Placeholder resets capped. Note in test they check `body.indexOf('Placeholder resets capped') !== -1`. Fine.

Is that intended? "say so ONCE" — the intent may be once per cap event. Minor issue: after the window resets (2h quiet), the count goes to 0; if placeholders persist and resets burn the cap again, no new park note is posted because placeholderParked is true from the old note. This is a minor observability gap — SUGGESTION level. Actually arguably intended ("say so ONCE"). I'd note as suggestion.

Both suites pass. Now let me check AGENTS.md conventions briefly and then examine remaining issues:

1. Check AGENTS.md for JS conventions.
2. Look at the full run_all? Not necessary — targeted suites pass.

Now let me consolidate findings:

**Findings to classify:**

1. **Redundant check-run fetches per tick** (SUGGESTION): in the placeholder flow, `headPlaceholders` is called up to 3 times per tick for the same head (green-cover guard ~line 2020, latch-skip guard ~2093, dispatch gate ~2322), each doing a fresh `github_get_commit_check_runs` REST call (headCheckRunsSafe has no caching). The comment at line ~1974 even says "ONE probe bundle feeds every guard below (was up to 4 sequential gh api rounds per candidate)". This PR adds up to 2-3 more sequential rounds in the placeholder-pinned path. Suggest caching the rollup per (head) per tick. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT? It costs API rounds on a hot path; the gh-842 work explicitly reduced rounds. I'd say IMPORTANT leaning SUGGESTION... It's a real perf regression in the exact pathological case only (placeholder-pinned PRs, which are rare and capped). And gate path only when placeholders detected. Actually green-cover guard path: for every skipIfGreenCi green PR, one extra check-run fetch per tick (headPlaceholders only when no zombies — zombies fetched first anyway which pre-existed). The added cost is 1 extra fetch per green PR per tick in the common case. SUGGESTION.

2. **Mixed zombie+placeholder head falls to legacy same-sha dispatch** (SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT): guards only probe placeholders when `zombies.length === 0`. A head carrying both a run-id ghost AND a placeholder would take the gh-842 same-sha re-dispatch, which can never cure the placeholder and may re-mint placeholders. Real? A head with a cancelled run ghost + placeholders is plausible (dispatch queued → placeholders minted; prior run cancelled). Design decision documented? The PR description says "Run-id zombies keep the legacy same-sha dispatch (AC3)" — deliberate for pure run-id ghosts. But mixed case silently picks the weaker remedy. IMPORTANT? Hmm. In mixed case, the legacy re-dispatch fires: if it materializes immediately, its fresh stamps override both ghosts (latest per context) — including placeholders IF the stamped contexts match the placeholder names. The placeholders carry names of required checks (e.g., 'Quality gate'), and stamped names are validationCheckNames() — likely same names. So same-sha dispatch with immediate start could cure. But if it queues, fresh placeholders re-minted. It's a partial-coverage edge case. I'd classify SUGGESTION (or low IMPORTANT). I'll go SUGGESTION with clear rationale.

3. **`hasPlaceholderZombies` exported but unused in production** (SUGGESTION): dead API surface — only the test references it. Either wire it into the gate (e.g., use in classify partition) or drop it.

4. **`placeholderParked` is sticky across windows** (SUGGESTION): once a park note is posted it never posts again, even after the window elapses and the cap re-arms; a second cap-hit storm gets silence. Probably "say so ONCE" intent, but worth noting.

5. **DRY check placement** (SUGGESTION): the DRY guard sits after the cap check and pool probe — in DRY mode the engine still performs comment reads and a repo-wide workflow-runs API probe before logging "skipped". Moving the DRY check first would avoid the API calls. Note: cap check in DRY reads comments — harmless but unnecessary. Minor.

6. **`silentUpdateBranch` no-op (already up to date) leaves head unchanged** — then dispatch happens on the same head with placeholders still pinned; the reset is counted against the cap anyway (marker posted) although no fresh sha was minted. Next tick re-detects placeholders, burns another cap. Edge case: branch already contains main but placeholders persist. Mitigated by pool probe (immediate-start dispatch cures). Still, counting an un-minted reset against the cap could burn the budget without a head move. Hmm — is that reachable? validate rules exclude BEHIND PRs; a PR whose branch already contains main and is not BEHIND... "already up to date" means main is ancestor of HEAD — that IS up-to-date (not BEHIND). So yes reachable: placeholders on a fresh-up-to-date head → silent update no-ops → same-sha dispatch (pool-free, so likely immediate start; run stamps override placeholders). If it materializes, cured. If the dispatch itself queues despite a free pool (runner labels unavailable — the pool probe is repo-wide ANY active run, quite conservative; a free pool read strongly suggests materialization)... acceptable. SUGGESTION at most. Actually the marker counting: marker posted counts a reset that didn't mint a fresh sha. Minor; mention in same comment as no-op handling. I'll fold into a SUGGESTION.

7. **`repoPoolFree` perPage 50** — newest 50 runs repo-wide; active runs are by definition recent, so coverage is fine. Skip.

8. **Fail-closed probe** — good.

9. **Security**: silent update uses token URL with env var — existing pattern. `dispatchCiWorkflow` command interpolates branch name into shell — existing pattern, branch names from GitHub data; pre-existing. No new secrets logged. OK.

10. **`placeholderMarks` counting**: marker regex `at (\S+)` — ISO from toISOString fine. Human-edited markers could game the cap, but this is a storm guard, not security. OK.

11. **Wait — one potential real issue**: In the gate, `failMarkerState(effectiveRepoInfo, ticket.prNumber)` is called on every tick when placeholders exist. But also, earlier in the flow, `redHeadBlocked` was already called (if enabled) which fetches comments separately (redHeadMarkerState). Two comment fetches per tick in that path. Pre-existing pattern for red heads; placeholder path adds one more. Combined with point 1. Minor.

12. **AC verification**:
- AC1: ✔ gate implements cap → pool probe → silent update → re-read head → dispatch → stamp → arm → marker.
- AC2: ✔ cap per PR per window + pool probe (fail closed).
- AC3: ✔ run-id ghosts keep legacy dispatch; tests cover.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI
